pathway.title: Fortrea Holdings Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the binding constraint, and even the house-adjusted measure leaves it high. Reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million gives net leverage of 9.12x and total debt leverage of 11.53x, and the house-adjusted measure that adds back restructuring, an Analyst Judgement, still gives 6.73x and 8.51x, with pro forma house-adjusted leverage not established; pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, net debt is USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x on reported EBITDA. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 77.8 million only 1.18x, and if the USD 150.0 million interest rate swap hedges the term loans, a 100 bp rise on the USD 422.00 million of floating debt it does not cover would add about USD 4.22 million of interest and cut cover to 1.12x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C1; calculation C4

Covenant headroom cannot be measured, but the stated compliance implies covenant EBITDA far above reported EBITDA, and the test tightens within weeks. The maximum Total Leverage Ratio is 5.75x at September 30, 2026, 5.50x at December 31, 2026, which is 43 days after the as-of date, and 5.30x after that; the issuer also says it must keep a net leverage and an interest coverage ratio and prints no level for the latter. If the test is on net debt, covenant EBITDA would need to be at least USD 145.17 million at 5.75x, USD 53.67 million above reported EBITDA, and USD 158.85 million at 5.50x on pro forma net debt of USD 873.7 million. The issuer states compliance and allows add-backs it does not print, so the gap is add-backs of unknown size; stock compensation of USD 50.80 million over the last twelve months added to house-adjusted EBITDA would bring net leverage to 4.78x. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

Free cash flow is not a dependable source of repayment. Last twelve months free cash flow of USD 169.0 million, after USD 32.8 million of capital spending and USD 77.8 million of cash interest, includes USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow, USD 132.8 million of it in the fourth quarter of 2025, so free cash flow before working capital is USD 23.5 million, 25.68% of reported EBITDA. Customers and a receivables sale fund the business from outside the debt, with unearned revenue of USD 525.5 million and USD 300.0 million of receivables sold, and cash taxes of USD 14.50 million are paid despite pre-tax losses. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C5

Revenue visibility is thinning and rests on few customers, which makes it the primary operating risk. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% to USD 4,390.7 million at September 30, 2026, backlog fell to USD 7.3 billion after a USD 558 million reduction, and the revenue contracted for the next 12 months is about USD 1,142 million, about 43% of last twelve months revenue. One customer was 17.2% of nine-month revenue and the top twenty were 69% of 2025 revenue, while most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

Margins have improved through cost actions, but from a thin base and by a route that is less repeatable than volume growth. Segment operating income more than doubled to USD 108.7 million in nine months as selling and administrative costs fell, reported EBITDA reached USD 91.5 million over the last twelve months from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026, and the 3.43% EBITDA margin is thin because 37.28% of nine-month 2026 revenue is pass-through cost that earns nothing. Restructuring charges have recurred every year, USD 44.1 million in 2025 and USD 10.1 million in nine months 2026, so part of the saving was bought with cash charges. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C10

Liquidity is adequate for the next 12 months but does not cover the 2028 maturities without a refinancing. Cash of USD 220.6 million and USD 447.7 million of undrawn revolver give USD 668.3 million before the acquisition's cash payment, which Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash; USD 387.5 million of term loan A and the USD 450.0 million revolver fall due on June 30, 2028, about 19 months away, and cash is 0.57x the term loan A balance. The revolver and term loan A enter their final 12 months on June 30, 2027, USD 649.0 million follows in 2030, and no rating, price or sponsor is supplied to show whether the market will refinance a business at this leverage. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; calculation C7

Financial policy has been creditor-friendly in conduct but brings no outside support. No sponsor stands behind the debt, no dividend has been paid, USD 75.7 million of notes were repurchased from disposal proceeds under the indenture and covenant relief in 2025 was paid for with a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens. Governance risk is Medium on the evidence, driven by turnover in the finance role in 2026 and an activist agreement, not by any creditor-adverse action. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C11

Claims outside reported debt and the quality of the balance sheet widen the leverage picture. Adding the USD 300.0 million of receivables sold to net debt of USD 834.7 million, which is USD 873.7 million pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, gives USD 1,134.7 million, or 12.40x reported EBITDA and 9.15x house-adjusted EBITDA; operating leases add USD 63.1 million, the UK pension plan has a small funding surplus, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,521.9 million exceed equity of USD 532.3 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 179; calculation C6

runs.text: Liquidity is the strongest support. Cash of USD 220.6 million and an undrawn USD 447.7 million revolver, with USD 2.3 million of letters of credit, give USD 668.3 million, before the acquisition's cash payment that Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash, which is 6.04x a year of cash interest and capital spending together, and nothing was repaid or drawn in nine months 2026. That means debt service through 2027 does not depend on a refinancing, which lowers near-term default risk as long as the revolver stays available. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7

Cost actions have lifted margin, and low capital intensity lets the gain reach cash. Segment operating income of USD 108.7 million in nine months is 101.30% above the prior year and selling and administrative costs fell 9.33%, while capital spending is 1.26% of revenue, so if volume holds the saving converts to cash that can repay debt, although restructuring recurs every year. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C10

Contracted revenue gives time to adjust. Backlog of USD 7.3 billion is 2.74x last twelve months revenue and remaining performance obligations are USD 4,390.7 million, so a downturn would work through the income statement over several quarters, not at once, which gives management room to cut cost before covenants tighten, although most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

Conduct has favoured creditors. No dividend has been paid, USD 75.7 million of notes were repurchased from disposal proceeds under the indenture and the 2024 term loan paydown was USD 482.7 million, so cash has stayed in the business, which supports deleveraging if earnings hold; the absence of a sponsor means no leakage but also no equity support. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; calculation C11

Leverage against earnings is the weakest point. Net debt of USD 834.7 million is 9.12x reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million (USD 873.7 million and 9.55x pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition) and cover of cash interest is 1.18x, so a small fall in earnings removes interest cover and tightens covenant tests that step down to 5.50x at December 31, 2026 and 5.30x after. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C1; calculation C3

Customer concentration makes earnings fragile. One customer was 17.2% of nine-month revenue and the top twenty were 69% of 2025 revenue, and because selling costs are largely fixed the loss of the largest customer's work would remove about USD 91.98 million of contribution, which is roughly all of reported EBITDA, an Analyst Judgement that overstates the loss to the extent the revenue is pass-through. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C8; calculation C9

Free cash flow depends on working capital. Last twelve months free cash flow of USD 169.0 million includes USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow and is USD 23.5 million before it, so repayment capacity from operations is small and a reversal of the USD 525.5 million of unearned revenue would draw on cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5

The 2028 maturities and the covenant step-downs create a refinancing event. USD 387.5 million of term loan A and the USD 450.0 million revolver fall due on June 30, 2028 and cash is 0.57x the term loan A balance, so the business must refinance or extend at a leverage that the covenant steps and the absence of a sponsor, rating or price make hard to place. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7

Contracted revenue is eroding. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% in nine months and revenue contracted for the next 12 months is about 16% lower than at year end, so earnings could soften before the cost actions run out, and management turnover in the finance role adds execution risk at the point when lenders need reliable reporting. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; calculation C8

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The founding transaction is the June 30, 2023 spin-off from Labcorp, a pro-rata distribution of one Fortrea share for each Labcorp share. Fortrea incurred USD 1,640.0 million of term loans and notes at the spin, namely USD 570.0 million of 7.50% senior notes due 2030 issued on June 27, 2023, a USD 500.0 million first lien term loan A due 2028 and a USD 570.0 million first lien term loan B due 2030, alongside a USD 450.0 million revolving facility, and it paid USD 1,595.0 million to Labcorp. The separation agreement leaves Fortrea responsible for substantially all liabilities of its business and for the Labcorp obligations it assumed, Labcorp has indemnified Fortrea for certain liabilities without assurance that the indemnity will suffice, and the transition services agreement ended on June 30, 2025. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 163–164; calculation C12

Two later transactions reshaped the balance sheet. The sale of the Enabling Services segment to Endeavor Buyer LLC, an affiliate of Arsenal Capital Partners, was agreed on March 9, 2024 and closed in the second quarter of 2024 for USD 340.0 million, of which USD 295.0 million was paid at closing and USD 45.0 million arrived as milestone payments of USD 20.0 million in the first quarter of 2025 and USD 25.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company paid down USD 70.2 million of term loan A and USD 412.5 million of term loan B in 2024 and repurchased USD 75.7 million of the notes in the fourth quarter of 2025 under the indenture's asset sale covenant, leaving USD 494.3 million outstanding. Funding also comes from a three-year USD 300.0 million receivables securitisation entered on May 6, 2024 and amended on February 24, 2026 to end on February 23, 2029; it is fully used and gives the administrative agent rights after an adverse rating change by either of two agencies. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 154; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation C12

The only transaction after the latest balance sheet is the October 19, 2026 acquisition of the Early Phase Services division of Worldwide Clinical Trials for about USD 45.0 million: USD 41.0 million payable at closing and USD 4.0 million deferred until transition services end and no later than 12 months after closing, with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash from cash on hand and the purchase price allocation not yet complete. The filings show no new debt issue after the spin: financing cash flows were nil in the nine months to September 30, 2026 and revolving borrowings of USD 453.9 million in 2025 were repaid in the same year. The February 28, 2025 amendment raised the maximum Total Leverage Ratio to 6.00x for quarters through June 30, 2026, with step-downs to 5.75x, 5.50x and 5.30x, in return for a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens during the adjustment period. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C13

At September 30, 2026 principal outstanding was USD 1,066.3 million: USD 494.3 million of 7.50% notes due 2030, USD 417.3 million of term loan A due June 30, 2028 and USD 154.7 million of term loan B due June 30, 2030, with the USD 450.0 million revolving facility, due June 30, 2028, undrawn apart from USD 2.3 million of letters of credit, leaving USD 447.7 million available. The sources do not state the lien rank of the notes against the credit facilities or name the guarantors of either. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and period construction from the five issuer filings, with the balance sheet of 2026-09-30 as the latest and the acquisition of October 19, 2026 as a subsequent event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fortrea carries leverage that its earnings base supports only thinly, so creditors rely on liquidity and on maturities that begin to bite only in 2028 rather than on interest cover. At September 30, 2026 net debt was USD 834.7 million, which is 9.12x reported EBITDA for the last twelve months of USD 91.5 million, and that EBITDA covered cash interest 1.18x. The October 19, 2026 acquisition raises net debt to USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x, before any EBITDA the acquired business adds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA carries restructuring charges, and a house-adjusted measure that adds them back, an Analyst Judgement, gives EBITDA of USD 124.0 million and net leverage of 6.73x. The issuer states no EBITDA, covenant ratio or maturity schedule for September 30, 2026, so covenant headroom is not established and the lien ranking of the 2030 notes rests on conflicting labels. Free cash flow of USD 169.0 million over the last twelve months leans on USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA was negative in 2024 and 2025, at USD 76.6 million and USD 794.6 million below zero, so leverage on a reported basis has no meaning for either year; the 2025 figure carries a USD 797.9 million goodwill impairment. The recovery shows in the last twelve months: EBITDA rose from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026 to USD 91.5 million at September 30, 2026, while gross debt stayed at USD 1,055.3 million because no principal was repaid in nine months 2026. Leverage therefore moves only with earnings, and 11.53x total and 9.12x net remain high for a business whose cash interest was USD 77.8 million over the same twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover of 1.18x at September 30, 2026 compares with 0.87x at June 30, 2026 and a negative cover in 2024 and 2025, so reported EBITDA now pays the interest but with little margin. Cash interest paid fell to USD 77.8 million over the last twelve months from USD 91.2 million in 2025, which the quarterly report attributes to the partial repurchase of the 2030 notes in 2025, no revolver borrowing and lower effective rates on the term loans; the rest of the improvement in cover is EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 72.7 million in nine months 2026 exceeded the net loss of USD 36.2 million mainly because of non-cash charges, USD 59.4 million of depreciation and amortization and USD 36.0 million of stock compensation, while working capital added a net USD 12.7 million: unearned revenue added USD 51.0 million and payables USD 23.7 million, against USD 55.3 million absorbed by receivables. Unearned revenue stood at USD 525.5 million at September 30, 2026, a customer-funded float that reverses if new bookings slow, and a further USD 300.0 million of receivables are sold and kept off the balance sheet, so the debt lines understate the funding the business draws from outside them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow of USD 169.0 million over the last twelve months, after USD 32.8 million of capital spending and after cash interest, is well above reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million only because working capital contributed USD 145.5 million of the operating cash flow, USD 132.8 million of it in the fourth quarter of 2025; before working capital, free cash flow was USD 23.5 million. Operating cash flow of USD 262.8 million in 2024 was lifted in the same way by the sale of receivables under the receivables facility, which the 2025 annual report gives, with higher payments to suppliers, as the reason operating cash flow fell in 2025.

fields.value: Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 220.6 million of cash plus USD 447.7 million available under the undrawn revolver, equal to 0.63x of total debt. The revolver and term loan A mature on June 30, 2028, when USD 387.5 million of term loan A falls due on the schedule at year-end 2025, and USD 649.0 million of notes and term loan B follow in 2030; the receivables facility is fully used and ends in February 2029. About USD 39.0 million of the cash left on October 19, 2026 for the acquisition, which is kept out of the period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer states no EBITDA, so every EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, which includes restructuring and impairment charges; what the issuer's own definition would give is not established. A dash in a statement is carried as nil only where the printed totals confirm it. Depreciation and amortization in the 2024 cash flow statement of USD 86.9 million differs from USD 85.3 million in the income statement because the cash flow statement includes discontinued operations. Debt is the balance-sheet carrying value of USD 1,055.3 million, USD 11.0 million below contractual principal of USD 1,066.3 million, and the 2030 notes are labelled senior in the debt note and senior secured in the exhibit list.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a stressed reading is cash and time: cash rose by USD 46.0 million in nine months 2026 with nothing drawn on the revolver, and the first principal payment above USD 25.0 million falls in 2028. The evidence for it is that last-twelve-month free cash flow rests on working capital and on USD 51.0 million of unearned revenue growth in nine months, and that restructuring charges have recurred every year, so a slowdown in new business would remove the cash cushion before it lifted earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business model, transactions, ownership and control, operating model, history and governance behaviour from the five issuer filings and the source readiness review, with the October 19, 2026 acquisition treated as a subsequent event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fortrea is a single-segment clinical research provider spun out of Labcorp with no disclosed controlling holder, so creditors rely on management execution and customer demand rather than sponsor support, and that reliance looks fragile today. Backlog fell to USD 7.3 billion at September 30, 2026 after a USD 558 million reduction, one customer supplied 17.2% of nine-month revenue, and the finance chief role was disrupted by a court order in July 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ftre-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: the filings show no dividend, notes repurchased under an asset sale covenant and a covenant amendment bought with a fee, but also an activist cooperation agreement, a staggered board until 2028 and compensation changes approved while backlog was being written down. The evidence supports caution on management stability, not a finding of creditor-adverse conduct.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a scaled but thin-margin services model: many contracts are fixed-price or fee-for-service with a cap, and more than a third of revenue is pass-through cost. Fortrea sells clinical development, clinical pharmacology and consulting services under full service, functional service provider and hybrid models, earned 47.35% of 2025 revenue in North America, 31.27% in Europe and 21.37% elsewhere, and passed through costs equal to 37.73% of revenue that earn no margin, leaving segment operating income at 3.21% of 2025 revenue. Margin is therefore set by staff utilisation and pricing discipline on the remaining work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 152; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 184; calculation C8; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contracted revenue visibility is thinning faster than reported revenue. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% to USD 4,390.7 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and the share due within 12 months slipped from 29.3% to 26%, so revenue expected over the next 12 months from them is about USD 1,142 million, about 16% lower than at year end and about 43% of last twelve months revenue of USD 2,666.7 million. Most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice, so the USD 7.3 billion of backlog is a pipeline, not a claim on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying activity is steadier than the revenue line and margins have improved, but from a thin base. Nine-month revenue fell 2.7% to USD 2,006.2 million, yet USD 48.3 million of the USD 56.7 million decline is lower pass-through costs that earn no margin, so revenue excluding them slipped only 0.66%. Segment operating income more than doubled to USD 108.7 million from USD 54.0 million, helped by segment selling and administrative costs that fell 9.33% and by restructuring plans approved in the fourth quarters of 2024 and 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C2; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is the largest business risk to creditors, and it rose through 2025. One customer was 18.1% of 2025 revenue, against two at 14.3% and 10.5% in 2024, the top twenty customers reached 69% of revenue from 61% in 2023, and the largest customer was 17.2% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 18.5% of receivables at September 30, 2026. If its revenue earned the company-average contribution of 20.05%, losing it would remove about USD 69.20 million of contribution, 2.62x nine-month operating income of USD 26.4 million, an Analyst Judgement that overstates the loss to the extent the customer's revenue is pass-through.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Working capital is funded by customers and by a receivables sale that is fully used, so cash conversion depends on award flow and on the lender's rights after a rating change. Unearned revenue of USD 525.5 million is 2.38x cash of USD 220.6 million and has risen from USD 214.2 million at the end of 2023, and USD 300.0 million of receivables are sold, 46.79% of those still on the balance sheet. The February 24, 2026 amendment moved the facility's end to February 23, 2029 but gives the administrative agent rights after an adverse rating change by either of two agencies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 186–187; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is dispersed public equity with no disclosed controlling holder, so no sponsor stands behind creditors, yet the board is protected against takeover and has already been pressed by an activist. The board is divided into three classes until the 2028 annual meeting, charter amendments need 75% approval until then, and a rights plan with a 10% trigger ran from June 11, 2025 until it expired on June 10, 2026 without extension. A February 21, 2025 cooperation agreement gave Starboard Value LP a say in board composition. Holdings, director independence and committee membership are not established in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management stability is the weakest governance point. The chief financial officer role passed from Jill McConnell, who signed the quarterly report of May 2026, to Jason Knoblauch, whose appointment a prior employer challenged in court on July 6, 2026; a restraining order on July 25 led the board to name director David R. Smith interim chief financial officer from July 27, and Mr. Knoblauch signed the September report as chief financial officer after a settlement in August with no material impact. On October 23, 2026 the compensation committee approved reimbursement of private aviation for the chief executive of up to 50 flight hours a year, capped at USD 300,000, and accepted Mr. Knoblauch's waiver of a USD 1,250,000 cash inducement award in return for legal fee indemnity and the lapse of forfeiture provisions on his earlier pay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor treatment since the spin has been conservative on cash leaving the company, but leverage was set by the separation and covenant relief carried a price. Fortrea incurred USD 1,640.0 million of term loans and notes at the spin and paid USD 1,595.0 million, 97.26% of that, to Labcorp; since then it has paid no dividend, paid down USD 482.7 million of term loans in 2024 and repurchased USD 75.7 million of notes in the fourth quarter of 2025 under the indenture's asset sale covenant. The February 28, 2025 amendment raised the maximum Total Leverage Ratio to 6.00x for quarters through June 30, 2026, then 5.75x at September 30, 2026, 5.50x at December 31, 2026 and 5.30x after, in return for a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens during the adjustment period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition appetite is modest on the evidence: the only purchase the filings describe since the spin is the USD 45.0 million Early Phase Services division of Worldwide Clinical Trials, bought on October 19, 2026, with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash from cash on hand, 17.68% of September 30 cash, and USD 4.0 million deferred. One small cash deal does not establish a pattern, and the 2024 disposal of Enabling Services for USD 340.0 million narrowed the business to one segment rather than adding leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for monitoring in the audited statements but inconsistent on points creditors price. The annual report says the company has no off-balance sheet financing other than short term leases and letters of credit, yet it had sold USD 300.0 million of receivables that were removed from the balance sheet, and the 2030 notes are called senior notes in the debt note but senior secured notes in the liquidity discussion. The auditor reported on internal control over financial reporting, which management concluded was effective at December 31, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is operating momentum and the absence of creditor-adverse conduct. Segment operating income more than doubled in nine months, backlog of USD 7.3 billion is still 2.74x last twelve months revenue, management states that the USD 558 million reduction reflected scope and delivery estimates and not any recent material customer communication and expects no material effect on near-term revenue, the company reported compliance with all covenants at September 30, 2026, and the court case over the finance chief settled with no material impact while the securities class action was dismissed with prejudice on September 28, 2026. No dividend has been paid and the only acquisition was small and paid in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the next quarterly report shows backlog stabilising and the share of obligations due within 12 months back above 29.3%, if the largest customer's share of revenue falls without a loss of revenue, and if the proxy statement shows independent directors and no holder above 10%. It would worsen if backlog falls again, if the largest customer cuts or ends work, if the receivables agent's rating-change rights are triggered, or if the finance chief role changes hands again.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Medium sponsor and governance rating assumes no holder with influence beyond the activist agreement, but the sources print no holdings, director independence or committee structure, so a holder near the 10% level that triggered the former rights plan would raise the risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The concentration finding rests on percentages alone: no customer is named and no contract term, renewal date or termination right is stated, so a long-dated contract with the largest customer would lower the risk and a near-term expiry would raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by delivery model and by therapeutic area is not printed beyond one oncology share, so the statement that weaker functional service provider demand drives the decline rests on management wording and could prove wrong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reasons for the 2025 and 2026 officer changes, the August 2026 settlement terms and the June 2026 current report are not in the sources, so the management stability finding rests on dates and exhibit titles and could be harsher or milder once they are read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The acquired division's revenue, earnings and purchase price allocation are not stated, so whether the October 2026 deal changes the operating model or adds earnings is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Backlog is defined by management and no net new business or book-to-bill figure is printed, so whether the USD 558 million adjustment signals customer attrition rather than estimation is not established; attrition would lower the view on revenue visibility further.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The founding transaction is the June 30, 2023 spin-off from Labcorp, a pro-rata distribution of one Fortrea share for each Labcorp share. Fortrea incurred USD 1,640.0 million of term loans and notes at the spin, namely USD 570.0 million of 7.50% senior notes due 2030 issued on June 27, 2023, a USD 500.0 million first lien term loan A due 2028 and a USD 570.0 million first lien term loan B due 2030, alongside a USD 450.0 million revolving facility, and it paid USD 1,595.0 million to Labcorp. The separation agreement leaves Fortrea responsible for substantially all liabilities of its business and for the Labcorp obligations it assumed, Labcorp has indemnified Fortrea for certain liabilities without assurance that the indemnity will suffice, and the transition services agreement ended on June 30, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two later transactions reshaped the balance sheet. The sale of the Enabling Services segment to Endeavor Buyer LLC, an affiliate of Arsenal Capital Partners, was agreed on March 9, 2024 and closed in the second quarter of 2024 for USD 340.0 million, of which USD 295.0 million was paid at closing and USD 45.0 million arrived as milestone payments of USD 20.0 million in the first quarter of 2025 and USD 25.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company paid down USD 70.2 million of term loan A and USD 412.5 million of term loan B in 2024 and repurchased USD 75.7 million of the notes in the fourth quarter of 2025 under the indenture's asset sale covenant, leaving USD 494.3 million outstanding. Funding also comes from a three-year USD 300.0 million receivables securitisation entered on May 6, 2024 and amended on February 24, 2026 to end on February 23, 2029; it is fully used and gives the administrative agent rights after an adverse rating change by either of two agencies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only transaction after the latest balance sheet is the October 19, 2026 acquisition of the Early Phase Services division of Worldwide Clinical Trials for about USD 45.0 million: USD 41.0 million payable at closing and USD 4.0 million deferred until transition services end and no later than 12 months after closing, with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash from cash on hand and the purchase price allocation not yet complete. The filings show no new debt issue after the spin: financing cash flows were nil in the nine months to September 30, 2026 and revolving borrowings of USD 453.9 million in 2025 were repaid in the same year. The February 28, 2025 amendment raised the maximum Total Leverage Ratio to 6.00x for quarters through June 30, 2026, with step-downs to 5.75x, 5.50x and 5.30x, in return for a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens during the adjustment period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At September 30, 2026 principal outstanding was USD 1,066.3 million: USD 494.3 million of 7.50% notes due 2030, USD 417.3 million of term loan A due June 30, 2028 and USD 154.7 million of term loan B due June 30, 2030, with the USD 450.0 million revolving facility, due June 30, 2028, undrawn apart from USD 2.3 million of letters of credit, leaving USD 447.7 million available. The sources do not state the lien rank of the notes against the credit facilities or name the guarantors of either.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by turnover in the finance role and board entrenchment alongside an activist agreement, because those facts weaken reporting continuity and holder discipline, which implies closer monitoring of covenant certification and capital allocation. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends, repayment of debt from disposal proceeds, settled litigation and effective internal control. No sponsor is disclosed, so fund vintage, sponsor equity contribution and sponsor fees do not apply. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Holdings, director independence and committee membership are not in the sources and the sources do not state whether Labcorp kept any shares after the spin, so the control and alignment of the board and the indemnity counterparty are not established. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the 2026 proxy statement and the registration statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The largest customer is not named, no contract term, renewal date or termination right is stated, revenue by delivery model, service and therapeutic area is not printed beyond one oncology share and no seasonal pattern is quantified, so concentration is sized by percentage only and the cause of the 2026 revenue decline rests on management wording. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain customer disclosures, an earnings release or a lender presentation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reasons for the 2025 and 2026 officer changes, the August 2026 settlement terms and the June 2026 current report are not supplied, so the management stability view rests on dates and exhibit titles. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the current reports and their exhibits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The acquired division's revenue, earnings, debt and purchase price allocation are not stated, and USD 41.0 million payable at closing is not reconciled with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash. Severity: Minor. Action: Use the next quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No net new business award or book-to-bill figure is printed, so the USD 558 million backlog reduction cannot be split into attrition and estimation. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the earnings release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement, indenture and receivables purchase agreement are not supplied, so capacity under restricted payment, investment and lien baskets is not assessed, the subsidiary guarantors are named only as a class and the receivables agent's rating-change rights cannot be read. Severity: Material. Action: Obtain the executed documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating is supplied and the two agencies named in the receivables agreement are not identified, so the rating-change right cannot be sized. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain rating reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Nothing dated after October 29, 2026 is supplied, so later events, including a third-quarter earnings release, cannot be excluded. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain filings dated after October 29, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall credit profile, strongest support and primary downside path from the five issuer filings and the supplied readiness, financial and business analyses, with the October 19, 2026 acquisition treated as a subsequent event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fortrea's fundamental credit is weak: net debt of USD 834.7 million at September 30, 2026 is 9.12x last twelve months reported EBITDA, so creditors rely on liquidity and a 2028 refinancing rather than on cash flow. Pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, net debt is USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is liquidity of USD 668.3 million before the acquisition's cash payment, with only scheduled amortization of up to USD 25.0 million a year before June 30, 2028. The weakest points are one customer at 17.2% of revenue, backlog cut to USD 7.3 billion and free cash flow of USD 23.5 million before USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow. The primary downside path is loss of work from the largest customer, which would remove contribution of about USD 91.98 million, roughly all of reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the binding constraint, and even the house-adjusted measure leaves it high. Reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million gives net leverage of 9.12x and total debt leverage of 11.53x, and the house-adjusted measure that adds back restructuring, an Analyst Judgement, still gives 6.73x and 8.51x, with pro forma house-adjusted leverage not established; pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, net debt is USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x on reported EBITDA. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 77.8 million only 1.18x, and if the USD 150.0 million interest rate swap hedges the term loans, a 100 bp rise on the USD 422.00 million of floating debt it does not cover would add about USD 4.22 million of interest and cut cover to 1.12x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant headroom cannot be measured, but the stated compliance implies covenant EBITDA far above reported EBITDA, and the test tightens within weeks. The maximum Total Leverage Ratio is 5.75x at September 30, 2026, 5.50x at December 31, 2026, which is 43 days after the as-of date, and 5.30x after that; the issuer also says it must keep a net leverage and an interest coverage ratio and prints no level for the latter. If the test is on net debt, covenant EBITDA would need to be at least USD 145.17 million at 5.75x, USD 53.67 million above reported EBITDA, and USD 158.85 million at 5.50x on pro forma net debt of USD 873.7 million. The issuer states compliance and allows add-backs it does not print, so the gap is add-backs of unknown size; stock compensation of USD 50.80 million over the last twelve months added to house-adjusted EBITDA would bring net leverage to 4.78x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is not a dependable source of repayment. Last twelve months free cash flow of USD 169.0 million, after USD 32.8 million of capital spending and USD 77.8 million of cash interest, includes USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow, USD 132.8 million of it in the fourth quarter of 2025, so free cash flow before working capital is USD 23.5 million, 25.68% of reported EBITDA. Customers and a receivables sale fund the business from outside the debt, with unearned revenue of USD 525.5 million and USD 300.0 million of receivables sold, and cash taxes of USD 14.50 million are paid despite pre-tax losses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue visibility is thinning and rests on few customers, which makes it the primary operating risk. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% to USD 4,390.7 million at September 30, 2026, backlog fell to USD 7.3 billion after a USD 558 million reduction, and the revenue contracted for the next 12 months is about USD 1,142 million, about 43% of last twelve months revenue. One customer was 17.2% of nine-month revenue and the top twenty were 69% of 2025 revenue, while most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have improved through cost actions, but from a thin base and by a route that is less repeatable than volume growth. Segment operating income more than doubled to USD 108.7 million in nine months as selling and administrative costs fell, reported EBITDA reached USD 91.5 million over the last twelve months from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026, and the 3.43% EBITDA margin is thin because 37.28% of nine-month 2026 revenue is pass-through cost that earns nothing. Restructuring charges have recurred every year, USD 44.1 million in 2025 and USD 10.1 million in nine months 2026, so part of the saving was bought with cash charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next 12 months but does not cover the 2028 maturities without a refinancing. Cash of USD 220.6 million and USD 447.7 million of undrawn revolver give USD 668.3 million before the acquisition's cash payment, which Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash; USD 387.5 million of term loan A and the USD 450.0 million revolver fall due on June 30, 2028, about 19 months away, and cash is 0.57x the term loan A balance. The revolver and term loan A enter their final 12 months on June 30, 2027, USD 649.0 million follows in 2030, and no rating, price or sponsor is supplied to show whether the market will refinance a business at this leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has been creditor-friendly in conduct but brings no outside support. No sponsor stands behind the debt, no dividend has been paid, USD 75.7 million of notes were repurchased from disposal proceeds under the indenture and covenant relief in 2025 was paid for with a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens. Governance risk is Medium on the evidence, driven by turnover in the finance role in 2026 and an activist agreement, not by any creditor-adverse action.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside reported debt and the quality of the balance sheet widen the leverage picture. Adding the USD 300.0 million of receivables sold to net debt of USD 834.7 million, which is USD 873.7 million pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, gives USD 1,134.7 million, or 12.40x reported EBITDA and 9.15x house-adjusted EBITDA; operating leases add USD 63.1 million, the UK pension plan has a small funding surplus, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,521.9 million exceed equity of USD 532.3 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 179; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak view is recovery and time. Reported EBITDA rose from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026 to USD 91.5 million at September 30, 2026, cash rose by USD 46.0 million in nine months with no revolver borrowing, house-adjusted net leverage fell to 6.73x from 18.53x at the end of 2025, before any effect of the acquisition, backlog of USD 7.3 billion is still 2.74x last twelve months revenue, the issuer states compliance with all covenants at September 30, 2026 and no principal above USD 25.0 million falls due before 2028. Capital spending of 1.26% of nine-month revenue also leaves little to fund, so a stable top line would let cost savings reach cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the fourth-quarter report shows backlog stabilising, free cash flow before working capital rising above USD 23.5 million without a further working capital inflow, the issuer printing its covenant ratio with headroom at the 5.50x and 5.30x steps, and an extension of the 2028 maturities. It would worsen if the largest customer cuts work, if unearned revenue falls below USD 525.5 million, if the receivables agent's rating-change rights are triggered, or if the 2028 maturities remain unaddressed when they enter the 12-month window on June 30, 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant requirement of USD 145.17 million of EBITDA at 5.75x assumes a net debt test and no netting limits, so a gross debt test or a different EBITDA definition would move the implied add-backs and could show real headroom or none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA and no guidance, so leverage rests on derived and house-adjusted measures; an issuer-adjusted figure above USD 124.0 million would lower leverage and weaken the conclusion that no supported measure removes it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario halves the largest customer's work and holds selling costs fixed, both assumptions without a management plan to test them, so the contribution lost, USD 45.99 million, could be materially higher or lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating, share price, bond quote or peer data is supplied, so the refinancing conclusion is not tested against market pricing, and a par-priced bond or a strong equity value would lower the 2028 refinancing risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The last twelve months free cash flow depends on a fourth-quarter 2025 working capital inflow whose reversal or repeat in the fourth quarter of 2026 is not visible, so the finding that cash flow is undependable could change with the year-end report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The interest rate swap's maturity and the loans it hedges are not stated, so the 100 bp sensitivity of USD 4.22 million could be understated if the swap expires or the notional covers other debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the strongest support. Cash of USD 220.6 million and an undrawn USD 447.7 million revolver, with USD 2.3 million of letters of credit, give USD 668.3 million, before the acquisition's cash payment that Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash, which is 6.04x a year of cash interest and capital spending together, and nothing was repaid or drawn in nine months 2026. That means debt service through 2027 does not depend on a refinancing, which lowers near-term default risk as long as the revolver stays available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost actions have lifted margin, and low capital intensity lets the gain reach cash. Segment operating income of USD 108.7 million in nine months is 101.30% above the prior year and selling and administrative costs fell 9.33%, while capital spending is 1.26% of revenue, so if volume holds the saving converts to cash that can repay debt, although restructuring recurs every year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contracted revenue gives time to adjust. Backlog of USD 7.3 billion is 2.74x last twelve months revenue and remaining performance obligations are USD 4,390.7 million, so a downturn would work through the income statement over several quarters, not at once, which gives management room to cut cost before covenants tighten, although most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conduct has favoured creditors. No dividend has been paid, USD 75.7 million of notes were repurchased from disposal proceeds under the indenture and the 2024 term loan paydown was USD 482.7 million, so cash has stayed in the business, which supports deleveraging if earnings hold; the absence of a sponsor means no leakage but also no equity support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage against earnings is the weakest point. Net debt of USD 834.7 million is 9.12x reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million (USD 873.7 million and 9.55x pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition) and cover of cash interest is 1.18x, so a small fall in earnings removes interest cover and tightens covenant tests that step down to 5.50x at December 31, 2026 and 5.30x after.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C1; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration makes earnings fragile. One customer was 17.2% of nine-month revenue and the top twenty were 69% of 2025 revenue, and because selling costs are largely fixed the loss of the largest customer's work would remove about USD 91.98 million of contribution, which is roughly all of reported EBITDA, an Analyst Judgement that overstates the loss to the extent the revenue is pass-through.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow depends on working capital. Last twelve months free cash flow of USD 169.0 million includes USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow and is USD 23.5 million before it, so repayment capacity from operations is small and a reversal of the USD 525.5 million of unearned revenue would draw on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2028 maturities and the covenant step-downs create a refinancing event. USD 387.5 million of term loan A and the USD 450.0 million revolver fall due on June 30, 2028 and cash is 0.57x the term loan A balance, so the business must refinance or extend at a leverage that the covenant steps and the absence of a sponsor, rating or price make hard to place.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contracted revenue is eroding. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% in nine months and revenue contracted for the next 12 months is about 16% lower than at year end, so earnings could soften before the cost actions run out, and management turnover in the finance role adds execution risk at the point when lenders need reliable reporting.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fortrea is a global contract research organization that runs phase I to IV clinical trials, clinical pharmacology and consulting for pharmaceutical, biotechnology and medical device customers under full service, functional service provider and hybrid models, in one reporting segment. It was spun out of Labcorp on June 30, 2023 and sold its Enabling Services segment in 2024, so the issuer is a three-year-old entity whose operating history before mid-2023 is carve-out data. Revenue was USD 2,666.7 million over the last twelve months, split about 47% North America, 31% Europe and 21% elsewhere in 2025, and 37.73% of 2025 revenue was pass-through cost that earns no margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 152; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business model supports cash-flow visibility through multi-year contracts, remaining performance obligations of USD 4,390.7 million and backlog of USD 7.3 billion, but most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice, one customer is 17.2% of revenue and the top twenty are 69%, so visibility is real but conditional. It weakens refinancing confidence because earnings depend on a few customers' research budgets, and it supports liquidity because customers pay in advance, with unearned revenue of USD 525.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fortrea is a public company with dispersed ownership, listed on Nasdaq, and no controlling holder or sponsor is disclosed. Fortrea Holdings Inc. owns Fortrea Inc., the operating subsidiary that conveys receivables to a special purpose entity under the receivables facility; the credit facilities have named obligors including an English borrower, and no guarantor is named in the filings. Structural priority between the notes and the first-lien term loans, and between parent and subsidiary claims, is not established because the legal documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance behaviour is mixed rather than adverse: no dividend, notes repurchased with disposal proceeds and covenant relief paid for with a fee and tighter limits, against an activist agreement, a staggered board until 2028, turnover in the finance role in 2026 and an executive compensation change approved in October 2026. With no sponsor, creditors get no equity cure, so liquidity and operations must carry any stress, and the Medium governance risk level in Business & governance supports monitoring of covenant reporting and capital allocation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows the conversion of backlog into work, the volume of customers' trials, and pass-through costs that move revenue without moving profit. Revenue was USD 2,842.5 million in 2023, USD 2,696.4 million in 2024 and USD 2,723.4 million in 2025, and nine-month 2026 revenue fell 2.7% to USD 2,006.2 million, but USD 48.3 million of the USD 56.7 million decline was lower pass-through, so revenue excluding it slipped 0.66%. Management attributes the 2026 decline to lower clinical development revenue and weaker demand for functional service provider work, partly offset by clinical pharmacology.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is not evidenced. Many contracts are fixed-price or fee-for-service with a cap, which leaves cost overruns with Fortrea, customers can end most contracts on 30 to 90 days notice or internalise functional service provider resources, and management cites price competition as a risk. Revenue is therefore contract-backed but cancellable, concentrated, partly pass-through and cyclical with customers' research budgets, not structurally declining; the implication is that volume loss, not price, is the mechanism that would move earnings and cash first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mainly people and pass-through: direct costs, including pass-through, were 79.9% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 81.9% a year earlier, and segment selling and administrative costs fell 9.33% as restructuring actions took effect. The filings do not split costs into fixed and variable, but the stated contribution after direct costs of 20.05% of revenue, with selling costs largely fixed, means each USD 100 million of lost revenue removes about USD 20.05 million of EBITDA before any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against a modest volume fall because restructuring has already cut selling costs and capital spending is flexible, but not against the loss of a large customer, wage inflation or adverse mix: merit wage increases and higher variable compensation partly offset savings in 2026, and restructuring charges of USD 32.5 million over the last twelve months show the cost base is still being reset. The implication is that margin resilience depends on volume, which is the weakest part of the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low: capital spending was 0.93% of 2025 revenue and 1.26% of nine-month 2026 revenue, so EBITDA converts to cash with little reinvestment, and spending of USD 32.8 million over the last twelve months leaves limited room to cut. Conversion is poor for other reasons: cash interest was USD 77.8 million, cash taxes USD 14.50 million and restructuring cash payments USD 23.6 million in nine months 2026, so free cash flow before working capital is USD 23.5 million, or 25.68% of reported EBITDA and 18.95% of house-adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Working capital swings dominate: USD 145.5 million of inflow lifted last twelve months free cash flow to USD 169.0 million, USD 132.8 million of it in the fourth quarter of 2025, and receivables of USD 300.0 million are sold off the balance sheet while unbilled services are 81.99% of gross receivables, so cash depends on billing milestones and customer advances. The implication for debt service is that free cash flow can repay debt only if working capital does not reverse, and the maturity wall in 2028 arrives before earnings-based free cash flow has had time to build.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and is the force that most affects margin: the industry is highly fragmented, with hundreds of small providers and a few large full-service ones, consolidation is led by the larger providers, and price competition could reduce revenue and profitability, which matters because segment margin is only 5.42% of nine-month revenue. Buyer power is high and is the second material force: customers are concentrated, most contracts end on 30 to 90 days notice and large pharmaceutical customers seek significant research cost reductions, so cancellations and price pressure transmit directly to revenue and cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The other three forces are secondary for credit. Substitutes exist where customers use in-house departments or internalise functional service provider resources; new entrants are not evidenced as a source of pricing pressure in the sources; supplier power sits with clinical sites, investigators and technology vendors and, for labour, with wage inflation, which affects cost but is not quantified. None of these changes the conclusion that rivalry and buyer power determine margin durability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two factors are material to credit. Economic conditions matter because customers' research budgets and biotechnology funding set demand: management says biotechnology funding slowed in the first half of 2025 and strengthened in the second half, and forecasts research spending by large biopharmaceutical companies to grow about 4% to 5% a year over 2025 to 2030 while the contract research market grows more slowly in the short term, so demand is cyclical and a funding slowdown would show first in new awards and cancellations. Regulation matters because the industry is subject to extensive rules with penalties for violations, but the company states it is in compliance in all material respects and no regulatory proceeding is disclosed. Social and technological factors, including artificial intelligence investment, do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the evidence supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: liquidity of USD 668.3 million before the acquisition's cash payment and only scheduled amortization of up to USD 25.0 million a year before June 30, 2028; cost actions that lifted segment operating income by 101.30% in nine months; contracted backlog of USD 7.3 billion; low capital intensity; and creditor-friendly conduct with no dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weaknesses: net leverage of 9.12x on reported EBITDA and 6.73x on a house-adjusted basis; interest cover of 1.18x; a largest customer at 17.2% of revenue; free cash flow of USD 23.5 million before working capital; and no sponsor, rating or price to support refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Opportunities: a stable top line would let cost savings reach cash and bring adjusted leverage toward the covenant steps; the early-phase acquisition adds clinical pharmacology capacity in the segment management says is growing; and an extension of the 2028 maturities would remove the main refinancing risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats: loss or reduction of work by the largest customer; further backlog adjustments; a reversal of customer advances; the covenant steps to 5.50x and 5.30x; rating-change rights of the receivables agent; and turnover in the finance role during the refinancing window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions the profile is weak overall. Scale and market position are average: revenue of USD 2,666.7 million is sizeable, but market share and peers are not supplied. Competitive advantage is weak on the evidence, because the margin fell from 5.97% in 2023 to 3.21% in 2025 and backlog and obligations are shrinking. Business diversification is weak: one segment and a concentrated customer base, with geography the only broad spread. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since capital spending is 1.26% of revenue and selling costs have been cut, but personnel-heavy direct costs follow revenue down slowly. Margin stability is weak, with reported EBITDA negative in 2024 and 2025 and USD 91.5 million over the last twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is weak, because USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow separates free cash flow of USD 169.0 million from USD 23.5 million before it. Ability to refinance is weak: leverage of 9.12x, maturities from June 30, 2028 and no sponsor, rating or price. Liquidity position is average: USD 668.3 million is ample for 12 months but the revolver ends with the term loan A maturity and its use depends on covenants. Financial policy and governance are average: conduct has favoured creditors, but the finance role has turned over and covenant relief was needed. The trend is improving from a low point, the main supports are liquidity, cost actions and contracted revenue, the main constraints are leverage, concentration and the 2028 wall, and the key missing datapoints are the covenant ratio and definition, the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, ratings and market prices.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outcome turns on three observable events: the covenant tests of December 31, 2026 and 2027, which step to 5.50x and 5.30x; the fourth-quarter report, which shows whether backlog and obligations stabilise after the USD 558 million reduction and whether the year-end working capital pattern repeats; and the handling of the 2028 maturities, which enter their final 12 months on June 30, 2027. A tailwind is the continuing effect of restructuring that runs through 2026 and lower interest after the notes repurchase; a headwind is the loss of work from concentrated customers, which management does not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years, management expects research and development spending to grow and outsourcing to remain elevated, but also says the contract research market will grow more slowly in the short term. Sector tailwinds are growing pipelines, complex trials and a recovery in biotechnology funding; sector headwinds are slower growth, price competition and customer consolidation. For credit the implication is that the 2030 maturities of USD 649.0 million fall in a period when sector growth could help earnings, but only if the 2028 refinancing succeeds first and leverage has fallen toward the covenant level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside begins with the largest customer halving its work, which the backlog adjustment and the 30 to 90 days termination rights show is possible. On 17.2% of last twelve months revenue, that removes USD 229.34 million of revenue; at the 20.05% contribution rate and with selling costs fixed, contribution falls by USD 45.99 million, taking reported EBITDA to USD 45.51 million and house-adjusted EBITDA to USD 78.01 million. Cover of cash interest falls to 0.58x reported and 1.00x adjusted, house-adjusted net leverage rises to 10.70x, and free cash flow before working capital turns to an outflow of USD 22.49 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity does not break first: cash of USD 220.6 million, before the acquisition's payment that Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash, covers the outflow for years, and if unearned revenue fell by 10%, USD 52.55 million, the annual outflow of USD 75.04 million would still be covered for 2.94 years by cash alone. The break comes through leverage and refinancing: covenant tests at 5.50x and 5.30x would be harder to meet, which could block the revolver, and cash of USD 220.6 million is USD 166.90 million short of the USD 387.50 million of term loan A due June 30, 2028, so the business would need a refinancing from a weaker position. Management levers are selling and administrative cost cuts, capital spending of USD 32.8 million, the absence of dividends and the revolver; resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not to repay the 2028 maturities without refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Fortrea presents a weak business profile supported by liquidity of USD 668.3 million, cost actions that doubled segment operating income and USD 7.3 billion of backlog, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 9.12x reported EBITDA, a largest customer at 17.2% of revenue and free cash flow that depends on working capital. Cash-flow durability appears weak because USD 23.5 million of free cash flow before working capital must carry USD 77.8 million of cash interest through a business whose revenue is cancellable. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovery toward the covenant steps, extension of the June 30, 2028 maturities and the absence of a rating-change event for the receivables facility.

fields.value: Primary downside path: loss of work from the largest customer removes contribution that is about equal to reported EBITDA, covenant tests tighten and the 2028 maturities cannot be repaid from cash. Business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the covenant ratio and definition, the executed credit documents, the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, ratings and market prices, the proxy statement and the fourth-quarter report. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: customer concentration feeding into leverage and the 2028 refinancing.
